decisions.reason: A schlager compilation CD costs little to keep listed in a large warehouse-backed catalog, and with no clear evidence of failure the option is worth keeping open, although stock may eventually run out.
The illustrated series builds on the label's core reissue competence and spreads its value across several models, so keeping the line open is cheap and preserves further upside.
Reissued jazz vinyl often comes in limited pressings that can sell out, but while stock remains, listing it costs almost nothing and it serves collector demand.
Multi-disc box sets are flagship catalog items for collectors and usually stay available for years, so dropping one would forgo value while holding it costs little.
A compilation CD close to the core offer is cheap to keep in stock, and the missing archive data reveals nothing negative enough to justify abandoning it.
